heroHeadline: Artemis Accords Reach 66 Nations as IFT-12 Counts Down to May 12 Launch — Starship Docking Hardware Test Imminent
heroSubtitle: May 5–6: Ireland signed the Artemis Accords on May 4 as the 66th signatory (24th ESA member state), following Malta (65th, early May) — three new nations joined in under two weeks as international momentum from Artemis II's successful crewed lunar flyby (April 1–10) accelerates global buy-in. NASA released more than 12,000 high-resolution images from the Artemis II mission on May 5, the largest deep space human mission imagery archive ever published, including close-up lunar surface photography, Earth-rise views from cislunar space, and crew documentation from the 10-day 252,706-mile journey. At Starbase, SpaceX's Starship Flight 12 (IFT-12) stands 6 days from its primary May 12 launch window — Ship 39 (Starship V3) and Booster 19 are stacked on Pad 2; IFT-12's first-flight validation of docking port and propellant-transfer hardware is the critical next step for Artemis III HLS qualification. At Kennedy Space Center, day 35–36 post-Artemis II splashdown operations continue: Orion heat shield visual inspection advances at the Multi-Payload Processing Facility while formal X-ray scans remain scheduled at Marshall Space Flight Center for summer 2026; Artemis III SLS core stage integration progresses in the VAB. The Artemis II crew (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen) continue week-5–6 physiological reconditioning at JSC with metrics largely normalized. In Congress, bipartisan opposition to the proposed 23% FY2027 NASA budget cut (47% science) has intensified across both the Senate CJS (Moran+Van Hollen, April 28) and House Science Committee, with appropriators signaling they will restore substantial funding as in prior years.
